name: NEAR Shoemaker
tagline: First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and the first to land on one, 433 Eros
description: NEAR Shoemaker, launched as Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous (NEAR), is NASA's spacecraft that orbited and then landed on the asteroid 433 Eros, the first mission of the Discovery program. The Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory built it. It launched on a Delta II 7925-8 from Cape Canaveral on 1996-02-17 with a mass of 805 kg, carrying five instruments and a radio science experiment. It flew past the asteroid 253 Mathilde on 1997-06-27 at about 1,200 km and past Earth for a gravity assist on 1998-01-23. After an aborted engine burn in 1998 delayed its arrival by about a year, it entered orbit around Eros on 2000-02-14, the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid, and returned about 160,000 images. On 2001-02-12 it touched down on Eros, the first landing on an asteroid, although it was not designed as a lander. Its last contact was on 2001-02-28.
best_known_for: First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and to land on one
